Eighth TU reconstruction pilot (ov002/daChScene_c). Reached TEXT-VERIFIED, 9/9 MATCH, objisolate clean, on the first verify pass -- no iteration needed despite this being the largest/most complex TU in the series so far (Behavior 0x304 bytes of real gameplay logic: player-crossing detection, camera cues, fader wipes, actor search). include/daChScene_c.h was a FLAT, non-inheriting header before this pilot (like daCamTag_c pre-fix) -- fields duplicating dActor_c's own mPosX/mScaleX/mAngleX/mHorzSpeed/param1 layout were re-declared rather than inherited, with no destructor and non-virtual methods. Extended it to `struct daChScene_c : dActor_c` with a real virtual destructor and the five real fBase_c-slot overrides, keeping every one of the class's own extensive field-reuse documentation (mScaleX as trigger-box half-width, mScaleZ as last-frame player z, mAngleZ as the exit band, mHorzSpeed as pull-through depth, etc.) verbatim since those notes describe values, not storage. One rename fell out of switching to real inheritance: the flat header's own `mParam` field is fBase_c's real `param1` (0x008, inherited transitively) -- InitResources and Behavior's four `mParam` reads were renamed to `param1` to resolve, matching the base's own field name rather than keeping a locally-invented alias. Two other TU-generator conflicts, both resolved: (1) `InvMat4x3`'s two legacy declarations disagreed on parameter ORDER (`in,out` vs `out,in`), but every call site in this TU passes the SAME pointer for both arguments, so the disagreement is byte-neutral -- kept one declaration, noted why. (2) `func_ov002_020b0a0c`'s legacy definition took a local shadow `struct Obj*` reading raw offsets 0x8/0x90, conflicting (illegal function overloading) with decl_common.h's own `void*` declaration of the same extern "C" symbol -- kept the void* boundary (matching decl_common.h and this function's only other caller, all within this same TU) and cast to `daChScene_c*` INSIDE the function body instead, replacing the raw-offset shadow struct with real `self->param1`/`self->mAngleZ` member access. Standard fixes otherwise: deleted the hand-written D0 body (real-D1-plus-hand-written-D0 mwcc ICE, fourth confirmed occurrence) and RESTORED the `+2` vtable addend on the factory's own store, which the legacy file had dropped (seventh confirmed occurrence). The store is `p[0] = (int)(_ZTV11daChScene_c + 2)`: the vptr points at the vtable's address point, two words past its start, exactly as at src/game/actors/d_a_ch_room.cpp:89. An earlier wording here said the addend was deleted; it was added. SUPERSEDED BY THE RENAME AND PROMOTION -- see the RENAMED AND PROMOTED note below for what this manifest actually carries now. Two claims that stood here are dead. (1) `compiler_only_output` no longer covers a D2 deadstrip: the destructor is inline, mwcc emits no `_ZN11daChScene_cD2Ev`, and that row was removed; the list now holds nine vague-linkage RTTI records instead. (2) This note used to argue that the class's own `_ZTI`/`_ZTS` were left out of `externalized_output` because the ROM spelled the class `daChScene_c` while the decomp spelled it `Exit` -- a coined-name mismatch it deferred to a later phase. The rename settled that mismatch (commit `dc9d38431`), and the class's own `_ZTV`/`_ZTI`/`_ZTS` are now licensed in `compiler_only_output` like the six inherited ones, because naming the class put its key function in this TU. The original sentence is not quoted back here: `class_rename.py` substituted the new name into both halves of it, so the text on disk read that daChScene_c was a different string length than daChScene_c, which is not a claim anyone made.

Marked (RESOLVED) rather than deleted, so the record that two legacy files disagreed about these names survives. Checked by tools/check_tubuild_conflicts.py.

RENAMED AND PROMOTED. The coined name `Exit` was replaced by the cartridge's own: ov002 _ZTV at 0x021086b4 is preceded by offset-to-top 0 and _ZTI 0x02108674, whose three words are 0x0209a764 (__si_class_type_info vtable + 8), 0x02108680 (its _ZTS, reading `11daChScene_c`) and 0x0208e390 (_ZTI8dActor_c, arm9). ov002's symbols.txt already spelled the _ZTI/_ZTS pair daChScene_c while naming the adjacent vtable _ZTV4Exit, so the rename closed an existing inconsistency. The TU then moved from src_tu/actors/daChScene_c.cpp to src/game/actors/d_a_ch_scene.cpp (tools/tu_names.py candidate_stem) and is compiled and linked into the ROM; the nine legacy per-function sources are deleted and config/arm9/overlays/ov002/delinks.txt gives this one file the whole .text run. One source change was needed: `virtual ~daChScene_c()` became `virtual ~daChScene_c() {}` in include/daChScene_c.h. Out of line mwcc emitted D2, D0, D1; the ROM has D1 at 0x020b09b0 then D0 at 0x020b09d4 and no D2, and production isolation orders .text by emission, so the out-of-line spelling was refused even though match.py and objisolate both passed the object -- objisolate checks one object's relocations, not the order the linker sees. The D2 deadstrip row this manifest used to carry was removed because that symbol no longer exists. The lever is safe because daChScene_c is a leaf: scanning all 977 extracted/**/*.bin files for the word 0x02108674 finds exactly one hit, 0x021086b0, which is this class's own vtable slot. Naming the class also made its key function (InitResources -- the first DECLARED non-inline virtual) land here, so mwcc now emits the class's own _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS alongside the six inherited base-chain records; all nine are licensed in compiler_only_output with the cartridge address of their canonical copy. Proof: tools/rombuild.py -j16 at 106/106 exact, 100.000000%, mismatching 0, ROM identical to the tree's last stock build.
